setting: A student arrives early for the campus career fair and asks staff about check-in, dress code, and resume drops.
narrator_intro: Listen to a conversation between a student and a staff member at the campus career fair.

dialogue.speaker: speaker1
dialogue.text: Hi. I'm here for the career fair. Doors open at ten, right? I wanted to get a good spot in line for the tech companies.

dialogue.speaker: speaker2
dialogue.text: Students can enter at ten, but employer booths don't start conversations until ten-thirty. You can check in now and pick up a name badge.

dialogue.speaker: speaker1
dialogue.text: Do I need to register online first?

dialogue.speaker: speaker2
dialogue.text: If you already registered, just scan your QR code at that table. Walk-ups are allowed, but some employers only see pre-registered students for interviews.

dialogue.speaker: speaker1
dialogue.text: I'm in business casual. Is that okay, or should I run back for a blazer?

dialogue.speaker: speaker2
dialogue.text: Business casual is fine for most booths. Engineering and startups are more relaxed; consulting tables prefer jackets, but you won't be turned away.

dialogue.speaker: speaker1
dialogue.text: Where do I drop paper resumes if a company isn't taking them at the booth?

dialogue.speaker: speaker2
dialogue.text: Use the resume drop boxes along the back wall—they're labeled by industry. Don't leave stacks on the tables; staff clear those.

dialogue.speaker: speaker1
dialogue.text: Is there a bag check? I brought a backpack with my laptop.

dialogue.speaker: speaker2
dialogue.text: Yes, free bag check by the east entrance. Keep your phone and a few resumes with you. The fair closes at three; interviews upstairs run until five.

dialogue.speaker: speaker1
dialogue.text: Perfect. I'll check in and grab a badge.

narrator_outro: Now get ready to answer the questions.

questions.narrator_text: What is the conversation mainly about?

options.B: How to check in and navigate the campus career fair
options.C: Buying business clothes at the campus store

questions.explanation: She arrives for the career fair; he explains entry time, registration, dress, resumes, and bag check.
questions.commonMistake: Choosing C—dress code is only one detail.

questions.narrator_text: When can students enter, and when do booth conversations start?

options.A: Enter at nine; conversations at nine-thirty
options.B: Enter at ten; conversations at ten-thirty
options.C: Enter at ten-thirty; conversations at noon
options.D: Enter anytime; conversations only after three

questions.explanation: Students enter at ten; employer booths start conversations at ten-thirty.
questions.commonMistake: Choosing C—ten-thirty is when talks start, not when doors open.

questions.narrator_text: What should she do with paper resumes if a company will not take them at the booth?

options.A: Leave them on any empty table
options.B: Mail them after the fair only
options.C: Use the labeled resume drop boxes along the back wall
options.D: Give them all to the bag-check attendant

questions.explanation: Drop boxes along the back wall are labeled by industry; tables get cleared.
questions.commonMistake: Choosing A—he warns not to leave stacks on tables.

questions.narrator_text: Until what time do upstairs interviews run?

options.A: Until three, when the fair floor closes

questions.explanation: The fair closes at three, but interviews upstairs run until five.
questions.commonMistake: Choosing A—confuses fair floor closing with interview end time.
